# Job queue design

The queue stores each job as a row with a lease expiry. Workers claim a job by setting the lease to now plus 30 seconds, and a heartbeat extends it every 10 seconds.

If a worker dies, its lease lapses and another worker can claim the job again. This gives at-least-once delivery, so handlers must be idempotent.

Retries use exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds and doubling up to a ceiling of 5 minutes. After 8 failed attempts the job moves to the dead letter table.

Operators can replay dead letters with the requeue command. Replayed jobs keep their original idempotency key so duplicates are dropped.

Metrics are exported as Prometheus gauges: queue depth, oldest job age, and lease expiries per minute. An alert fires when the oldest job age exceeds 10 minutes.

The schema migration adds a partial index on status so that claiming scans only runnable rows, which cut claim latency from 40 ms to 3 ms in testing.

# Licensing summary

The core library is released under the Apache 2.0 license, which permits commercial use, modification and distribution, and includes an explicit patent grant.

The command line tool is dual licensed. Individuals and companies under ten employees may use it under the MIT license. Larger organisations need a paid commercial agreement.

Contributions require signing a contributor agreement that assigns copyright to the foundation. Pull requests without it are not merged.

Trademarks are separate from code licensing. The logo and name may not be used to imply endorsement without written permission.

Documentation is published under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, so it can be copied with credit.

Security reports go to a private address and receive an acknowledgement within 48 hours. Fixes are disclosed after 90 days or on release, whichever is first.
